statement: For every nonempty finite abstract simplicial complex G whose faces all have cardinality at most two, let L_G be the unweighted face-intersection matrix and D_G the unaugmented oriented-incidence Dirac matrix defined in problem.md. For every integer 1 <= k <= |G|, S_k(L_G) >= S_k(D_G) + 1, where S_k sums the k largest eigenvalues with multiplicity. The constant 1 is sharp, already at k=1 for the complex consisting of one edge and its two vertices. Disconnected complexes, isolated vertices, and non-bipartite graphs are included. This is only the dimension-at-most-one case; the original arbitrary-dimensional comparison remains unresolved.
contribution: A self-contained uniform proof of the author's previously conjectured additive-one bound for the entire graph-complex subclass, with sharpness. The proof combines the known unsigned incidence spectral transform with a degree-majorization and odd-cycle argument that handles signed Dirac spectra without assuming bipartiteness. No equivalent graph theorem was found in the primary sources and bounded searches recorded on 2026-09-14; priority and publication value require fresh review. The exact positive five-vertex census and numerical graph checks are supplementary evidence, not the basis of the infinite theorem.
